def test_port_boundary_and_errors(self):
        """Regression tests for port access on urlsplit and urlparse results."""
        for parse in (urllib.parse.urlsplit, urllib.parse.urlparse):
            # --- str URLs ---
            # No port: construction succeeds, port is None
            p = parse("http://example.com/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, None)
            # Empty port: construction succeeds, port is None
            p = parse("http://example.com:/:/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, None)
            # Port 0: accepted boundary
            p = parse("http://example.com:0/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)
            # Port 65535: accepted boundary
            p = parse("http://example.com:65535/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)
            # Port 65536: out of range
            p = parse("http://example.com:65536/")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                p.port
            self.assertIs(type(ctx.exception), ValueError)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                           ("Port out of range 0-65535",))
            # Negative port: not a valid digit string
            p = parse("http://example.com:-1/")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                p.port
            self.assertIs(type(ctx.exception), ValueError)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                           ("Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'",))
            # Noninteger port
            p = parse("http://example.com:abc/")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                p.port
            self.assertIs(type(ctx.exception), ValueError)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                           ("Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'",))
            # Non-ASCII decimal digit (Arabic-Indic digit 1)
            na_digit = "١"
            p = parse("http://example.com:" + na_digit + "/")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                p.port
            self.assertIs(type(ctx.exception), ValueError)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                           (f"Port could not be cast to integer value as {na_digit!r}",))

            # --- bytes URLs ---
            # No port
            p = parse(b"http://example.com/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, None)
            # Empty port
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:/:/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, None)
            # Port 0
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:0/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)
            # Port 65535
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:65535/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)
            # Port 65536: out of range
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:65536/")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                p.port
            self.assertIs(type(ctx.exception), ValueError)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                           ("Port out of range 0-65535",))
            # Negative port
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:-1/")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                p.port
            self.assertIs(type(ctx.exception), ValueError)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                           ("Port could not be cast to integer value as b'-1'",))
            # Noninteger port
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:abc/")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                p.port
            self.assertIs(type(ctx.exception), ValueError)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                           ("Port could not be cast to integer value as b'abc'",))
